status_summary: The removal tools the Foreword describes are in place: Schedule Policy/Career was reinstated by order on 2025-01-20, made at-will by OPM's final rule of 2026-02-06 and applied to listed positions by Executive Order 14410 of 2026-06-03 (see c03-01), and workforce reduction orders, an OPM reduction-in-force rule effective for notices on or after 2026-09-02 and an OPM administrative leave final rule published 2026-10-19 followed (see c03-06). Shuttering offices has begun with orders eliminating the non-statutory functions of eleven named entities in 2025 (see c03-09), while Federal News Network reported three lawsuits over the placements pending in July 2026 with no court rulings. The Supreme Court stayed an injunction against Executive Order 14210 on 2025-07-08, and an amended complaint against the placement order was reported on 2026-06-25; the stage is derived from the three detailed records.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14171 signed; it redesignates the 2020 Schedule F framework as Schedule Policy/Career and has agencies petition OPM to place positions in it.
Executive Order 14210 directs agency workforce reduction plans, sets a limit of one hire per four departures and directs agency reductions in force.

Executive Order 14217 signed (published 2025-02-25): directs elimination of the non-statutory functions of four named entities (Presidio Trust, Inter-American Foundation, U.S. African Development Foundation, U.S. Institute of Peace).

Executive Order 14238 signed (published 2025-03-20): directs the same treatment for seven further entities, including the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service, the U.S. Agency for Global Media, the Institute of Museum and Library Services and the Minority Business Development Agency.
Supreme Court (Trump v. AFGE, No. 24A1174) stays a N.D. Cal. injunction against Executive Order 14210, without ruling on specific reduction-in-force plans.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: The Ninth Circuit grants the government's motion to dismiss its own appeal (No. 25-7998) of the N.D. Cal. preliminary injunction of 2025-12-17 in AFGE v. OMB on shutdown-period reductions in force, by a clerk's order that constitutes the mandate (see c03-06).
timeline.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit (copy on storage.courtlistener.com)

timeline.event: OPM final rule on the Schedule Policy/Career framework published (effective 2026-03-09): covered positions stay career but are at-will, outside chapter 75 adverse-action procedures and MSPB appeals.

Executive Order 14410 signed (published 2026-06-10): places positions listed in an appendix in Schedule Policy/Career; press reports put the number at about 8,000 employees in more than 4,800 positions.

Bloomberg Government reports that the Government Accountability Project and the National Active and Retired Federal Employees Association have filed an amended complaint in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia challenging the 2026-06-03 placement order (about 8,000 employees) as exceeding presidential authority and violating the Civil Service Reform Act; the report gives no filing date (see c03-01).
OPM final rule on reductions in force published (91 FR 49178), effective for notices issued on or after 2026-09-02.
OPM proposes a rule, Employment in the Excepted Service (comments due 2026-11-17), updating excepted-service regulations to cover Schedule Policy/Career and Schedule G.

OPM publishes the final rule Administrative Leave for Workforce Realignment and Other Purposes (91 FR 65924, effective 2026-11-18), which clarifies when administrative leave may be used for deferred resignation programs and other workforce realignment and when it may be granted during a reduction-in-force notice period.

title: Fire un-fireable career bureaucrats and shutter wasteful federal bureaus and offices
uncertainties: Stage derivation: c03-01 is implemented 75, c03-06 is implemented 75, c03-09 is in_progress 30. The two firing-side records would support implemented, but the Foreword also asks to shutter bureaus and the detailed record on cutting duplicated functions is only in_progress 30, so the combined stage is in_progress 60, the top of the band. Implemented 65 is defensible. c03-07 (political appointees) was left out of restates_ids because the sentence is about removing bureaucrats, and appears in related_ids and in c00-20. The copy of c03-09 was not in the folder; its stage comes from the existing listing and the two entity-closing orders were read on federalregister.gov in this run. The number of employees affected by Executive Order 14410 comes from press reports cited in c03-01, not from the order. OPM's year-end 2025 statement that about 317,000 federal employees would leave in 2025 (over 90 percent through voluntary programs) is a statistical claim, not a government action, so it was moved out of the timeline; it includes voluntary departures, which are not removals. Searches on 2026-10-28 found no new ruling on Schedule Policy/Career placements or reduction-in-force plans. In review the court status was updated from the 2025-07-08 Supreme Court stay to pending, following the later court events verified in c03-06 (Ninth Circuit dismissal of 2026-01-02) and c03-01 (amended complaint reported 2026-06-25); the amended complaint's filing date is not stated in the report. A Federal News Network report of 2026-07-06 (close to 8,000 employees notified, three pending suits, no rulings) is a status report and is kept as a source rather than a timeline event. c03-06 also records the 2025-12-17 district court injunction on shutdown-period reductions in force (running through 2026-01-30), which is not repeated here.
